sourceConclusions: Importing supplier-owner and obs-client starts no process, opens no private state and makes no request. Root explicitly invokes startSupplier; child peer scripts are owned CLI entrypoints.
Fresh tags, private directories, exclusive0600 execution logs and fixed loopback ports prevent reuse of old private namespaces. Health binds scope/tag/source hash.
GH/K derivation diffs are limited to new M roots/names/ports/hosts/control/receipt prefixes and small readiness/owner wiring; no deep protocol semantics were silently rewritten.
Feishu callbacks remain confined to the frozen loopback endpoints; no actual vendor tenant or directory is addressed.
OBS retains exact key/byte-hash ownership, bounded control-token admission and zero-object/zero-active graceful shutdown before a valid stop receipt.
The owner retains exact source checks, uses the existing owned-process runtime and verifies released ports; there is no global process kill or old-instance stop.
actualUseBoundaries: Root must bind these exact source hashes in the current capsule and verify actual health, case registration, object ownership, drain and port release.

gracefulPeerReceipt means peer closure was acknowledged; it is not successful M5 business/protocol acceptance. Preserve Feishu peerStop.result and any failed assertion/forced stop as their actual labels.
A shutdown or zero-state failure must remain failure/partial. The finally-owned stop preserves data; it must not manufacture a clean or passed supplier case.
Cloud-peer objects and control journals require actual exact cleanup/second-zero proof under Root ownership before final stage acceptance.
Public projections and raw private logs stay separate; this source review exposes no credentials, tokens or old private content.
